story.title: Gérard Depardieu Ordered to Stand Trial for Rape and Sexual Assault
story.summary: Gérard Depardieu, the renowned French actor, has been ordered to stand trial for allegedly raping actress Charlotte Arnould at his Paris home in 2018. The Paris Court of Appeal upheld the decision, which comes shortly after Depardieu abandoned an appeal in a separate sexual assault conviction. If found guilty, he could face a significant prison sentence.

explore_lenses.label: How did the case reach this stage?
explore_lenses.title: A reopened complaint led to a long investigation
explore_lenses.summary: Arnould first complained in 2018, but the matter was initially closed; a subsequent complaint led to a judicial investigation and Depardieu's formal investigation status in 2020. An investigating judge ordered a trial in August 2025, which Depardieu appealed.

claims.text: Arnould's initial complaint was transferred to the Paris prosecutor and closed in June 2019; a new complaint led to appointment of an investigating judge, who placed Depardieu under formal investigation in December 2020.
The investigating judge's August 2025 order had sought a trial over alleged rapes on both August 7 and August 13, 2018; the appeal court narrowed that order to the first date.

This case is separate from Depardieu's May 2025 conviction for sexual assaults against two women on a 2021 film set; in November 2026 he withdrew his appeal in that case and accepted an 18-month suspended sentence.

explore_lenses.label: What happens before a trial can begin?
explore_lenses.title: A final appeal remains possible
explore_lenses.summary: Depardieu's lawyers said they would examine a possible appeal to France's Court of Cassation after receiving the written decision. If the case goes forward, it is assigned to a departmental criminal court, which hears serious crimes including rape allegations.

claims.text: Depardieu's lawyer said the defense would consider a Court of Cassation appeal once it receives the investigating chamber's decision; AFP also reported that the appeal-court ruling can be challenged through that procedure.

Under Justice Ministry guidance, a departmental criminal court can try crimes punishable by 15 to 20 years' imprisonment, including rape, and is composed of five professional judges; it determines guilt and any sentence after adversarial proceedings.
If there is a conviction or acquittal at the criminal-court trial, the defendant or prosecutor may appeal; the civil party may appeal only the civil-compensation component.

story_report.summary: A Paris appeal court has ordered French actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial over allegations that he raped and sexually assaulted actor Charlotte Arnould in 2018. Depardieu denies the allegations. The ruling means the case can proceed to a criminal trial, although it does not determine whether the alleged acts occurred or establish criminal liability; those questions remain for the court hearing the case.

sections.heading: Arnould Complaint and Investigation
sections.body: Arnould’s initial complaint was transferred to the Paris prosecutor and closed in June 2019. A subsequent complaint resulted in the appointment of an investigating judge, who placed Depardieu under formal investigation in December 2020. An August 2025 order sought a trial over alleged rapes on Aug. 7 and Aug. 13, 2018, but the appeal court narrowed the referral to the first date.

sections.heading: Depardieu Defense and Trial Process
sections.body: Depardieu’s lawyer said the defense would consider an appeal to the Court of Cassation after receiving the investigating chamber’s decision. If the case goes to trial, a departmental criminal court may hear rape cases punishable by 15 to 20 years in prison; it is composed of five professional judges and decides guilt and any sentence after adversarial proceedings. Either the defendant or prosecutor may appeal a conviction or acquittal.

sections.heading: Separate 2021 Film-Set Case
sections.body: The Arnould case is separate from Depardieu’s conviction in May 2025 for sexually assaulting two women on a 2021 film set. In November 2026, he withdrew his appeal in that case and accepted an 18-month suspended sentence.

unresolved.text: No trial date has been reported, and it is not yet known whether Depardieu will seek Court of Cassation review.
The competing accounts concerning consent and the question of criminal liability have not been resolved and remain for trial if the case proceeds.

related_stories.title: Fuel Truck Fire in Cairo Kills 31 and Injures 21
related_stories.summary: A fuel tanker overturned on a major highway near Cairo, igniting a massive fire that engulfed over two dozen vehicles. At least 31 people have died and 21 others were injured in the incident. Authorities have detained a driver suspected of causing the crash, who reportedly confessed to speeding and clipping the tanker while overtaking traffic.

related_stories.title: Diesel Tanker Capsizes Off Ibiza, One Crew Member Dies
related_stories.summary: A Maltese-flagged diesel tanker carrying approximately 7,000 tonnes of fuel capsized off the coast of Ibiza. While all 17 crew members were rescued, one later died in the hospital. Spanish authorities are now implementing a contingency plan to address potential marine pollution risks.
